title: The Hermit

seo.title: Destiny matrix 9 — The Hermit: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: 9 in the destiny matrix is The Hermit: depth and the search for meaning. We look at its strong and weak versions and how it differs from its neighbours.

meaning: The ninth arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of depth and the search for meaning. It is not enough for such a person to know that something works: they need to understand why, to reach the very root — and for that they walk away from the noise. The Hermit is not an unsociable character, it is a whole direction of life turned inwards.

The engine here is a question that will not let go. While other people move on, this one is still digging. The main inner conflict grows out of exactly that: depth needs solitude, but what depth produces needs people. Going into yourself is easy and familiar, bringing the finished thing out into the light is hard, and the arcanum spends its whole life on that seam.

To be the ninth arcanum means carrying constant quiet work inside, work that nobody outside suspects. The world feels too loud for what the person is looking for; depth and silence pull harder than any company. A pause before answering and distance taken in advance are not coldness, they are a way of living.

This energy has two versions, and from the outside they are easy to mix up. In the strong one the person runs their own solitude: they choose depth on purpose, dig out rare knowledge and share it with those who found their way to them. In the weak one the solitude runs the person — they once shut the door out of tiredness, coming back out gets harder every year, and the wall grows thicker without any decision being made. One slides into the other unnoticed, and the shift can only be caught from the inside.

What separates the ninth from its neighbours is precisely the silence. The eighth, Justice, gives its decision out loud — it weighs, judges and answers for its verdict in front of everyone; the ninth looks for the same truth in silence and finds it by stepping away from people. The tenth, The Wheel, catches the moment and the luck in it and moves on the wave of events; the ninth is indifferent to timing and keeps digging at its own slow pace, whatever the world around it is busy with.

article.title: Arcanum 9 in the destiny matrix — The Hermit: withdraw in order to return
article.short: 9 in the destiny matrix is The Hermit, the energy of knowledge a person wins for themselves: in silence, slowly and with no one handing them the answer. Nines know how to withdraw from the day they are born. Their real task begins afterwards: coming back to people with what they have understood, and sharing it.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 9: The Hermit — meaning, karmic tails and program 9
seo.description: Destiny matrix 9 is The Hermit, who withdraws in order to return. Find your nines by birth date in a minute, see why some charts have none, and read the tails.

sections.h2: What 9 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The nine is the energy of someone for whom knowing how a thing works is not enough: they need to understand why. A ready-made answer from someone else does not settle them, and until they have checked everything for themselves, the question stays open. That is why they step away from the noise. Not away from people as such, but away from the interference that stops them thinking a thought through. Hence the reputation of a silent loner, although for a nine solitude is not the goal but the workplace.

This energy has its own rhythm in three steps: **withdraw, work it out, come back**. The first two come easily to a nine; they are its nature. The third is the hardest, and that is where the meaning of the arcanum lies. What separates a strong nine from a weak one is not how closed off they are, but whether they ever get as far as coming back.

This is not a modern invention. Arthur Edward Waite, the author of the best-known Tarot deck, argued with the interpreters of his day: The Hermit is “a card of attainment”, not a card of quest. He is not wandering at random in search of truth; he has already arrived, and Waite put the meaning of the figure like this: “where I am, you also may be.” So the popular formula “the nine is the search for yourself” is only half right. The search is just the means. A mature nine is someone who has found the way and can show it to others.

Waite also rejected another version: that The Hermit stands for “occult isolation”, hiding to protect his “personal magnetism against admixture”. The mysteries, he wrote, “secure their own protection from those who are unprepared”: someone who is not ready simply will not take them in. For the matrix the practical conclusion is this: a nine does not need walls. Depth cannot be carried off by being shared, and a wall built “for protection” slowly ends up fencing the person off from their own life.
A nine rarely stands out. You recognise one by the small things:

ul: At a noisy party they find one person to talk to and spend half the evening on what really matters. Everyone else thinks they were bored; for them it was the best conversation in a month.
They reply to a message a day later, but to the point, and answer along the way the question you had not yet got round to asking.
Before a decision they gather information for so long that everyone around stops waiting. But a decision, once made, rarely has to be reversed.
They know their field more deeply than the job requires and say nothing about it. Colleagues find out how good they are by accident, when something breaks that nobody else can fix.
They give advice rarely and briefly, but people remember it years later.
They show care through action: they will find it, sort it out, mend it, and never mention it.
When tired, they do not complain; they vanish. For them it is a breather; for the people close to them it is a mystery, and sometimes a hurt.

paragraphs: A nine in one point of the chart does not have to show itself in everything at once. In one person it shows at work, in another only in love, in a third in the way they rest. Where exactly is told by the position; more on that below.

sections.h2: Arcanum 9 in plus and in minus: one energy, two ways to live it
paragraphs: There are no reversed cards in the matrix: a number calculated from a date cannot be turned upside down. “Plus” and “minus” are not two different arcana but two ways of living one and the same energy. For a nine, things can go wrong at any of the three steps, and each step has its own warning sign.

In plus

Sign that it is time to come out
rows: Withdraw

paragraphs: There is also a shadow that people rarely write about. In Waite’s divinatory list, next to prudence, The Hermit is given treason and dissimulation (the whole list is in the section on the card below). In the matrix this is neither a verdict nor a character trait but a hint at where a strength can turn. A person used to deciding everything in silence one day silently decides for others too. Quietly leaves a shared venture without a word of explanation. Keeps what they know to themselves, because knowledge gives power. Agrees out loud, then does it their own way. From the inside it is “I just didn’t feel like explaining”; from the outside it is a stab in the back.

The second trap is the arrogance of the self-taught. Benebell Wen, author of the book Holistic Tarot, describes the weak side of the card as someone who “thinks he or she knows best”, “can be petulant to elders” and to “those with more experience”, and “prefers to rely on his or her own mistakes and experience than to learn from others”. A nine is used to winning knowledge alone and easily forgets that asking someone who knows is also a way to the heart of things, and the shortest one.

sections.h2: The Hermit, The High Priestess, The Hierophant and The Moon: telling them apart
paragraphs: Three other arcana are also tied to hidden knowledge and depth, and the nine is often mistaken for them.

**The High Priestess (2)** is also silent and also knows more than she says. But her knowledge comes from within: by instinct, at once and without proof. The Hermit’s knowledge is earned through experience, testing and a long road. The High Priestess knows but cannot always explain how. The Hermit can tell you the whole route; he just will not tell it to everyone.

**The Hierophant (5)** is also a teacher, but he teaches by tradition, passing on what generations have accepted and tested: in a school, a community, a profession. The Hermit is a teacher without a school. Wen draws the line like this: The Hierophant “is about orthodox wisdom”, while The Hermit is “the unorthodox solitary path to wisdom”. The Hierophant cares that it is right; The Hermit cares that it is true.

**The Moon (18)** is the nine’s closest relative by number (1 + 8 = 9), and in the matrix the two keep standing side by side; why, you will see below. But they look in different directions. The Moon goes into the unclear by instinct and imagination, taking its fears along. The Hermit goes from the unclear towards the essence. The nine asks “how is it really?”, the eighteenth arcanum asks “what if?”.

If two of these energies stand together in your chart, the combination has a page of its own: [The High Priestess and The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/2-9), [The Hierophant and The Hermit](/encyclopedia/combination/5-9), [The Hermit and The Moon](/encyclopedia/combination/9-18).

sections.h2: Where 9 sits in the destiny matrix and how to find it from your birth date
paragraphs: The arcanum tells you what the energy is; the position tells you where it works. The nine is one of the most common energies: 81.2% of people have it in at least one section of the reading (across the arcana this share ranges from 13.4% to 85%). Some of the points can be checked from the date of birth without a calculator.

paragraphs: If the nine falls in several points, that does not make a “double Hermit”: each position is read separately, and in each one the energy solves its own task.

**People born in September** get the nine in several sections at once: point B is the spiritual task, the start of the talent line and the arcanum of the decade from 20 to 30. For those born on the 9th and the 27th, the nine leads the first decade of life; for those born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025, the decade from 40 to 50. The calculator works out the other points. The nine turns up even more often in the chakras, where 56.5% of people have it on at least one of the seven levels, and in the reading by decades (44.8%).

**The Hermit year** arrives by the calendar, not by age. Add the day of your birth (if it is greater than 22, add up its digits first) to the number of the month. If the sum is 17 or 26, 2026 is your year under the nine; if it is 16, 25 or 34, 2027 is. What to do in such a year is covered on the page [9 for the year](/year/9).

sections.h2: Why some charts have no nines and others are half nines
paragraphs: Nines are spread across charts unevenly, and you can check this in a minute. Add up all the digits of your date of birth. For 18.09.1980 that is 1 + 8 + 0 + 9 + 1 + 9 + 8 + 0 = 36.

ul: **The sum is not divisible by 3**: true for two thirds of people. Then there is no nine, and there cannot be one, in the centre, the karmic task, the karmic tail or any of the four purposes. If The Hermit is in your chart, it stands in the date points, the family lines, money, relationships, talents or chakras.
**The sum is divisible by 3 but not by 9.** At the entry of the karmic tail (point M) and in the spiritual purpose stands a 9 or an 18, The Hermit or The Moon, without exception.

**The sum is divisible by 9**: true for one person in nine. Nines and eighteens take the centre, the karmic task, all three numbers of the tail and all four purposes, and the tail is one of three: 18-9-9, 9-9-18 or 9-18-9.

paragraphs: The reason is the divisibility rule from school: a number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9. All the matrix does is add numbers and reduce them by their digits, so divisibility by 9 runs right through the calculation. And the tail entry and the spiritual purpose are built so that the sum of the date goes into them three times and six times, which is why divisibility by 3 is enough for them. The nine and the eighteen travel as a pair because they are the only arcana that are multiples of nine. For those who know numerology: the third group are people with Life Path number 9. The systems are different, but here their arithmetic agrees.

The extreme case is when the day, the month and the year are each divisible by 9 on their own: the 9th, 18th or 27th of September in a year whose digits add up to a multiple of nine (1908 and every nine years after it, up to 2025). Since 1900 there have been 42 such dates, and for these people the whole chart, every point, chakra and decade, consists of nothing but nines and eighteens. Someone born on 18 September 1980 has no energy in the matrix except The Hermit and The Moon.

sections.h2: 9 in the karmic tail: the six tails that carry The Hermit
paragraphs: The karmic tail is three numbers read in order: the entry (the first reaction), the mechanism (what it unfolds into) and the root (the task the whole story exists for). 21.4% of people have a nine in their tail: it appears in six of the 26 possible tails, and in five of them it stands at the entry. In each place it plays its own part:

ul: **at the entry**, the first move “I’ll deal with it myself, quietly”: faced with a difficulty, the person steps aside and works it out alone;
**in the middle**, the mechanism “not ready yet”: the working-out never ends, understanding piles up and stays inside;
**at the root**, the task of bringing what has been understood to people, so that it serves more than just you.

paragraphs: Each of the six tails with a nine is covered on its own page:

ul: [18-9-9](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/18-9-9): “Forbidden Knowledge”, the most common of the six, at 8.9% of birth dates. The person notices more than others but carries the hunch off to where nobody can check it.
[9-12-3](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-12-3): “The Lonely Woman”, though it falls to both genders (4.3%). Everything important is done alone and without words, and the unspoken request is left hanging.
[9-15-6](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-15-6): “A World of Passions and Fairy Tales” (3.4%). Whatever excites is carried off into secrecy, and the secret starts to hold on.
[9-3-21](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-3-21): “The Warden” (2.7%). Care that sees trouble before anyone else turns into supervision and control.
[9-9-18](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-9-18): “The Wizard” (2%). Preparation becomes a way of life, while the root demands a step into the unknown without waiting for full clarity.
[9-18-9](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/9-18-9): “The Magical Victim”, the rarest of the six (0.21%). In the silence, imagination assembles fears into a picture of someone else’s ill will.

paragraphs: The five tails with a nine at the entry share the same first move: not to speak but to go inwards. What differs is what grows in that silence: with The Hanged Man, an unspoken request; with The Devil, a secret passion; with The Empress, protective care; with The Moon, anxious guesses; with the second Hermit, endless preparation. So in all five the same first step helps: say out loud what you would normally settle in silence, before the second number has time to unfold.

And one more pattern. A nine in the centre of the chart comes only with the tails 18-9-9 and 9-9-18, and everyone who has these tails also has a nine in the centre. Know one, and you already know the other.

sections.h2: Program 9: the script that keeps coming round
paragraphs: “Program 9” usually means a nine in a karmic point of the chart. In our reading, the programs section reads three positions: the karmic task D, the centre E and the spiritual purpose. 27.4% of people have a nine in at least one of them, and only those whose date digits add up to a multiple of 3. How programs work in general and how they differ from character traits is explained on the page [programs in the destiny matrix](/programs).

The nine’s script is recognisable by its sequence. Things get hard or hurtful, and the person shuts themselves away to work it out alone. The working-out drags on, ties weaken, nobody calls. This is taken as proof: “nobody needed me anyway”. The next withdrawal goes deeper than the last. The loop feeds itself: the longer the silence, the more reasons there seem to be that there is no one to talk to.
It is broken not at the moment of leaving (a nine may withdraw, and should) but at the moment of return, while the pause is still short. Three moves that work:

ol: **Announce the end date in advance.** “I’m thinking it over on my own until Friday”: a named date turns a disappearance into a pause.
**Show unfinished work.** A fresh pair of eyes halfway along is worth more than one at a perfect finish you may never reach.
**Reach out the next day, not a month later.** After a month the silence needs explaining, and it is easier to stay silent.

paragraphs: How this story looks in the reading is shown in the section [“Programs: what repeats in circles”](/encyclopedia/position/loops).

sections.h2: Love, money and work with a nine in the chart
paragraphs: A nine loves faithfully, deeply and without show: attention comes through deeds rather than words, and one close person is enough for a long time. The difficulty lies in the pauses. When a nine needs to recover, they go inwards, and a partner who does not know this rhythm reads the silence as coldness or punishment. More on the pages [9 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/9) and [9 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/9).

If your partner has the nine, three things will help more than any talk about feelings. Do not coax them out of the silence; agree instead that they will tell you how long they are going away for. Ask their opinion on a matter, not about their mood: a nine opens up through whatever is occupying their mind. And do not mistake restraint for indifference; check against their actions, which in a nine are more honest than words.

A nine is paid for depth: expertise, rare skills, difficult cases, long work that never has to be redone. The bottleneck is selling themselves: the person does the job better than most and tells nobody. This applies to the whole money channel, including the point that other charts mark with a dollar sign. More: [9 in money](/encyclopedia/position/money/9).

The right work is where depth counts for more than speed and noise: research, analysis, editing and translation, programming, restoration, archives, expert assessment, crafts, teaching small groups, one-to-one consulting, writing. It is harder where you have to be on show all the time: cold calling, doorstep selling, an open-plan office with meetings about everything. More: [9 in talents](/encyclopedia/position/profession/9).

sections.h2: 9 in a man and in a woman
paragraphs: Gender plays no part in calculating the matrix: the same date of birth gives the same numbers to a man and to a woman. The meaning of the nine does not change with gender either: restraint, the need for silence and depth in work are found equally in both.

“Male” in the matrix is not the person’s gender but the family lines. The spiritual and material male family lines (points F and H) describe the father’s side, and the nine stands there for 6.0% and 7.7% of people of either gender. In this role it speaks of a principle handed down the father’s line: to value knowledge and work done above words. The strong side of this inheritance is a capacity for long independent work; the heavy side is a habit of keeping quiet where a conversation is needed. In the female family lines (points G and I) the nine occurs in 6.6% and 6.2% of people.
If you are looking this up because the nine belongs to the man in your life, go back to the paragraph about the partner above: it holds just as well for any gender.

sections.h2: 9 in compatibility: a couple under the sign of The Hermit
paragraphs: The compatibility matrix is a separate calculation: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22, which gives a third chart, the chart of the couple. There is no generally accepted method for reading it. Below is how Yuliana Lisovskaya describes the nine in a couple in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). This is her practice, not canon, and the method gives no compatibility percentages.

**What such a couple looks like.** Calm, quiet, modest. They tell people about events after the fact, once everything has already happened, and they are reluctant hosts. Each has their own time or their own corner for solitude, and nobody takes offence. Love is shown through deeds, they share a view of the world and learn from each other. The pace is slow in everything: a very long time can pass between the first date and the wedding.

**What feeds it.** Long conversations about what matters, trust, respect for boundaries, the partner’s foresight and patience. Such a couple happily spends money on books, courses and study; in everyday spending they are unhurried and almost always keep something in reserve.

**Where it gets hard.** Each lives their own life, and problems are not discussed but pile up. Work quietly takes the place of family, and there are fewer and fewer friends. Sometimes two people stay together not because they are happy but because they are afraid of being alone. From the outside such a couple looks cold, as if the partners came from different planets.
**The couple’s task** is not to snuff out each other’s interests, not to retreat into their shells when things get hard but to reach out, to do more together and to talk about whatever is piling up.
A curious detail: a couple’s matrix can have the tail 9-9-9, which never occurs in a personal chart. In Lisovskaya’s book it comes out for a couple with the birth dates 16.07.2003 and 01.09.2005.

sections.h2: Waite’s Hermit: what is on the card and what it means in a spread
paragraphs: On the card by Arthur Waite and Pamela Colman Smith, an old man in a grey hooded cloak stands on a snowy peak. In his right hand he holds up a lantern with a six-pointed star burning inside; in his left he holds a staff. His eyes are lowered: he is not scanning the road ahead but standing where others are still climbing to, holding up the light for them.

Waite himself explained what he had changed in the familiar image. In earlier decks the lantern is half hidden by the cloak, and the figure was often compared to Diogenes, who searched for an honest man with a lamp in broad daylight. In Waite’s deck the lantern is open, “it is a star which shines in the lantern”, and The Hermit himself stands on a height: hence “a card of attainment” and the words “where I am, you also may be”. In his figure, Waite says, the Ancient of Days, the image of God from the Book of Daniel, is blended with the Light of the World: “I am the light of the world,” Christ says of himself in the Gospel of John. Waite argued both with those who saw in the card a sage still in search of truth and with those who took the cloak for a shield against outside influence.

And earlier still there was no lantern at all. In fifteenth-century Italian decks the card was called Time, the Old Man or the Hunchback, and the old man held an hourglass. By the end of that same century the hourglass had given way to a lantern, and Time became The Hermit. Curiously, “Time” still describes the nine well: it measures its work in years, not weeks.

Another story has to do with the old virtues. There are four of them: Justice, Strength, Temperance and Prudence. The first three appear in the deck as cards of their own; the fourth does not. Éliphas Lévi gave Prudence to The Hermit; Waite remarked that this was done out of “the wish to fill a gap which would otherwise occur in the symbolism”, yet in his own divinatory list the word still comes first.

**In a Tarot reading** Waite’s upright Hermit means “prudence, circumspection; also and especially treason, dissimulation, roguery, corruption”. Reversed, it means “concealment, disguise, policy, fear, unreasoned caution”. Modern authors read the card more gently. Benebell Wen sees in it “guidance and mentorship” and introspection: either the person becomes the mentor, or they receive counsel from someone wiser. Reversed, for her it is “wise counsel” that the person “is not heeding”, and a sign that “greater introspection and wisdom is needed before a decision should be made”. Wen also links The Hermit with the sign of Virgo and the element of Earth.

For the matrix, one thing in all this matters: it has no reversed meanings. Waite’s dark list is not “the nine in minus” but a reminder of what the habit of settling everything in silence can turn into.

sections.h2: If 9 is in your matrix: what to do with it
paragraphs: A nine does not need to stop being itself; it needs to carry its cycle through to the end. A few habits that help this particular energy:

ol: **Withdraw with an end date.** “I’m thinking it over on my own until Friday”, and on Friday come back, even if you have not thought it all through. An incomplete conclusion shown in time is more useful than a complete one that nobody ever sees.
**Show unfinished work** to one person who is under no obligation to praise it. A nine tends to spend weeks polishing alone what a fresh pair of eyes would fix in a minute.
**Ask before you get stuck.** One question to someone who knows saves a month of digging on your own. It is not a defeat but a short road to the same essence.
**Voice disagreement out loud.** A silent “I’ll do it my way” looks like deceit from the outside, even if you simply did not want to argue.
**Tell silence from a wall.** The test is simple: “I’m quiet because I’m thinking” or “because I don’t want to see anyone”. The first is a resource; the second is a signal to come out.

**Find someone to pass it on to.** A nine does not need a crowd, but it does need at least one person who will have a use for its knowledge: a student, a colleague, a reader. Passing it on is the last step of its cycle, and without it what was found simply stays in the drawer.
